title: Hymns of the mind
hookLine: the mind is called restless, and the Word is its rest

lines: A MIND TRYING TO SOLVE ITSELF.
cards: It's the middle of the night, and a mind is trying to solve itself. It runs the plan again, the conversation again, the worst case again. Each time it gets a little cleverer, and a little less rested.
Guru Amar Das, in the Anand, his song of bliss, turns to exactly that mind: e man chanchala, O restless mind. Not to scold it. To tell it something it keeps missing about cleverness, and about rest.

teach.h: E MAN CHANCHALA: O RESTLESS MIND.
teach.b: Here's the verse, paraphrased: O restless mind, no one has found Him through cleverness.

Listen, my mind, no one has found Him through cleverness. This enticing Maya has led people astray in doubt. And the verse ends where it began: O restless mind, no one has found Him through cleverness.
Chanchal means restless, flickering, never still. The mind's favorite tool for getting still is cleverness: one more plan, one more argument, one more way of being sure.
The Guru says that tool doesn't reach the place the mind is trying to get to.

teach.h: SAID AGAIN, FOR A TIRED LISTENER.
teach.b: And he repeats the line, the way you'd say something twice to someone who's tired and not quite hearing you. So where is rest?
The Anand's opening verse points the way, again paraphrased: I have found the True Guru, with ease, and my mind rings with rejoicing; sing the Word, all of you who have let it dwell in the mind.

Rest, in that picture, comes through the Word. Not a new idea to win with, but the Guru's Word, heard, sung, remembered, until the mind stops having to hold itself up. You can't think your way into rest.
But you can rest in the Word.

how: The Anand Sahib, with its verses to the restless mind, is part of the Sikh daily banis, and its opening and closing pauris are sung at the end of gatherings at the gurdwara.

games.q: what does “hymns of the mind” mean?
o: verses telling the restless mind to rest in the Word
hymns that train the mind to win every argument
a set of puzzles meant to sharpen the intellect

games.q: the restless mind: tap the pairs.
p: never finds the Lord, the verse says
the enticement that leads astray in doubt

s: Guru Amar Das tells the restless mind to get cleverer
he says no one has found the Lord through cleverness.
the warning about cleverness is repeated within the verse
it comes back again, like something said twice to a tired listener.
in his hymns, rest comes through the Word
the Anand opens by calling those who keep the Word in the mind to sing it.

games.q: it's late, and the mind keeps solving the same problem. what does the Anand point to?
o: the Guru's Word, as the mind's rest.
games.why: cleverness never finds Him, the verse says; the Anand opens by calling those who keep the Word in mind to sing it.

practice: Choose one line from these days, man too jot saroop hai, by any door, or simply Waheguru, and let it ride the breath, in and out.
When the mind starts solving, planning or arguing, don't fight it with more cleverness; just lay it back down on the line, the way you'd lay a tired child back on a pillow. The line holds the mind.

wordCard.voice: Hymns of the mind. Guru Amar Das calls the mind restless, says cleverness never finds the Lord, and offers the Word as its rest. Today's word.

orig.note: restless, never still: how the Anand addresses the mind.

carryVoice: Your line: rest in the word. Cleverness keeps the mind up; the Word lets it lie down. Rest well tonight.
